name: UEFI & Secure Boot Assessment
description: Security assessment of UEFI firmware and Secure Boot implementations. Covers UEFI application analysis, Secure Boot bypass and key management, bootkit detection and development, firmware extraction and reverse engineering, TPM-backed Measured Boot evaluation, and boot chain integrity verification across Windows, Linux, and macOS platforms. Scope is PC/UEFI platforms; embedded and SoC boot chains belong to HWSEC-EMBED-BOOT.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to UEFI or Secure Boot security assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands UEFI architecture, Secure Boot, and boot chain concepts
evidence: Can explain UEFI boot process, Secure Boot key hierarchy (PK, KEK, db, dbx)
Understands the difference between BIOS and UEFI and security implications
Familiar with Measured Boot, TPM PCRs, and boot chain attestation concepts
Completed introductory training on UEFI security

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Extracts and analyzes UEFI firmware and Secure Boot configuration under supervision
evidence: Extracted UEFI firmware images using flashrom, CHIPSEC, or vendor tools
Analyzed Secure Boot key database and policy configuration
Reviewed UEFI variable storage for security-relevant settings under guidance
Work reviewed by authorized researcher

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses UEFI and Secure Boot implementations
evidence: Independently assessed Secure Boot configuration and identified bypass vectors
Extracts and analyzes UEFI DXE drivers and runtime services
Evaluates Measured Boot and TPM-backed attestation chains
Passed proficiency assessment on UEFI security

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Discovers UEFI vulnerabilities and evaluates bootkit resilience
evidence: Discovers vulnerabilities in UEFI DXE drivers or SMM handlers
Evaluates system resilience against known bootkit techniques (BlackLotus, FinSpy)
Performs UEFI firmware fuzzing and CHIPSEC-based security assessment
Mentors team on boot chain security methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on boot chain security; published UEFI vulnerability research
evidence: Published research or CVEs on UEFI or Secure Boot vulnerabilities
Developed lab methodology for boot chain security assessment
Contributes to Secure Boot policy and firmware security guidance
Trains teams and presents at conferences on UEFI exploitation

assessment_methods.description: Assess the UEFI and Secure Boot configuration of a prepared system, identify bypass vectors, and evaluate boot chain integrity
Given a UEFI firmware image, extract and analyze DXE drivers to identify potential vulnerabilities
